ranking_detail.mechanism: Cytoplasmic mislocalization of TDP-43 (TARDBP) causes nuclear loss-of-function that permits cryptic exon insertion into STMN2 and UNC13A pre-mRNAs, depleting functional stathmin-2 and Munc13A and driving motor neuron degeneration.

C9orf72-derived poly(GR)/poly(PR) dipeptides bind FG-repeat nucleoporins (NUP62) and RANGAP1, impairing KPNB1-mediated nuclear import and GLE1-dependent mRNA export, which drives TDP-43 nuclear depletion and a self-amplifying nucleocytoplasmic transport defect.

The nuclear m6A reader YTHDC1 functions as an RNA-independent molecular chaperone that suppresses aggregation of ALS-linked mutant hnRNPA1, so nuclear depletion or sequestration of YTHDC1 accelerates hnRNPA1 amyloid-like assembly and motor neuron death.

Mitochondrial dysfunction releases mtDNA that activates the CGAS-STING1-TBK1-IRF3 axis in microglia, inducing a neurotoxic type I interferon (IFNB1/ISG) program that STING inhibition can suppress to protect motor neurons.

ALS-linked KIF5A C-terminal variants and TDP-43-dependent disruption of the Miro (RHOT1)-TRAK2 kinesin adaptor reduce anterograde mitochondrial delivery to distal axons and NMJs, causing distal axonal energy starvation.

Biallelic loss of spatacsin (SPG11), the gene underlying ALS type 5, impairs autophagosome maturation and TFEB/LAMP1-dependent lysosomal trafficking, blocking aggregate and organelle turnover and accelerating proteinopathy in motor neurons.

Upregulated matrix metalloproteinase-9 in fast-fatigable motor neurons and muscle degrades synaptic basal lamina components (agrin, laminin-alpha2, collagen IV) at the neuromuscular junction, accelerating NMJ disassembly and denervation.

Dysfunction of SIGMAR1 and loss of the VAPB-PTPIP51 (RMDN3) ER-mitochondria tether uncouple ITPR3-mediated ER calcium release from MCU-mediated mitochondrial uptake, causing mitochondrial Ca2+ overload, mPTP-dependent death, and depressed oxidative phosphorylation.

Loss of the arginine-glycine-rich RNA-binding protein ARPP21 disrupts post-transcriptional regulation and localization of its target mRNAs in motor neurons, impairing neuronal translational programs and lowering the threshold for neurodegeneration.

Loss of alsin (ALS2) Rab5 GEF activity together with CHMP2B ESCRT-III dysfunction blocks RAB7A-dependent endosome-lysosome maturation and neurotrophin receptor (NTRK2/TrkB-BDNF) recycling and retrograde delivery, starving axons of trophic support.

Misfolded SOD1 variants (D90A, G93A) act as seeds that template strain-specific prion-like conversion of native SOD1 into aggregation-prone conformers, and stabilizing the native SOD1 dimer with small molecules such as NABi blocks seeded aggregation and slows motor neuron loss.

Astrocyte-secreted C1q and microglial C3 opsonize motor neuron synapses and neuromuscular junctions, promoting CR3 (ITGAM)-mediated microglial engulfment and premature denervation, so blockade of the C3-CR3 axis will preserve NMJ integrity.

Misfolded SOD1 and phosphorylated TDP-43 aggregates activate the microglial NLRP3 inflammasome, driving caspase-1-mediated GSDMD cleavage and release of IL-1β/IL-18 that accelerate motor neuron death, so NLRP3 or GSDMD inhibition will attenuate progression.

Repression of SLC7A11 (system xc-) with consequent GPX4 inactivation, combined with ACSL4-driven incorporation of polyunsaturated fatty acids into membranes and TFRC-mediated iron uptake, executes lipid-peroxidation-dependent ferroptotic motor neuron death.

Defective CCS-mediated copper loading and ATP7A-dependent copper trafficking leave SOD1 in the apo, aggregation-prone state, promoting misfolding that CuATSM copper delivery or SOD1 dimer-stabilizing aggregation inhibitors can rescue.

Downregulation of monocarboxylate transporter MCT1 (SLC16A1) in oligodendrocytes limits lactate export and metabolic coupling (with LDHA/PPARGC1A-dependent substrate supply) to motor axons, depriving axonal mitochondria of substrate and accelerating degeneration.

Impairment of the PINK1-PRKN (PARK2)-to-OPTN/TBK1 mitophagy axis in motor neurons causes accumulation of depolarized, ROS-producing mitochondria, producing progressive bioenergetic failure consistent with organism-wide energetic collapse.

Elevated CSF1 released from degenerating motor neurons and denervated muscle engages CSF1R on microglia and macrophages, driving proliferative expansion of pro-inflammatory APOE-high disease-associated microglia, so CSF1R inhibition will reduce microgliosis and slow progression.

Loss of astrocytic EAAT2 (SLC1A2) glutamate transporter expression and function reduces synaptic glutamate clearance, raising extracellular glutamate and driving motor neuron excitotoxic death along the riluzole-targetable axis.

Elevated circulating FGF2 signals through endothelial and pericyte FGFR1-ERK signaling at the blood-spinal cord barrier, destabilizing VE-cadherin (CDH5) and occludin (OCLN) junctions, increasing permeability and permitting peripheral immune-cell infiltration that FGF2/FGFR1 blockade can reverse.

RAN-translated poly(GA) dipeptide-repeat proteins from the C9orf72 expansion directly inhibit PSMB5 proteasome catalytic activity and overwhelm aggregate-clearance capacity, producing gain-of-function proteotoxic stress that kills motor neurons.

Loss of suppressive FOXP3-positive regulatory T cells (reduced IL-10/TGF-β tone) skews peripheral immunity toward Th1/Th17 effectors whose IFN-γ and IL-17A license microglial activation and CD8-positive T-cell motor neuron cytotoxicity, so low-dose IL-2 or Treg restoration will be protective.

Misfolded SOD1 and TDP-43 seeds are packaged into ESCRT-dependent CD63-positive exosomes whose biogenesis requires neutral sphingomyelinase (SMPD3), enabling prion-like cell-to-cell propagation of proteinopathy along motor pathways that exosome-biogenesis or seed-uptake blockade can slow.

Increased IL-6/soluble IL6R trans-signaling through IL6ST (gp130)-JAK-STAT3 in motor neurons and glia sustains a neurotoxic inflammatory state, so sgp130Fc-mediated blockade of IL-6 trans-signaling will attenuate STAT3 activation and motor neuron injury.

Reduced neuronal CX3CL1 fractalkine presentation to microglial CX3CR1 (with altered ADAM10-dependent shedding) weakens the anti-inflammatory neuron-microglia checkpoint and amplifies microglial IL-1β/TNF-α output, so restoring CX3CL1-CX3CR1 signaling will protect motor neurons.

HMGB1 released from necrotic motor neurons engages TLR4 and RAGE (AGER) on microglia and endothelial cells, sustaining RELA/NF-κB-driven cytokine production and secondary excitotoxic injury, so HMGB1 neutralization or TLR4 antagonism will break the inflammatory amplification loop.

Injury-induced CCL2 from motor neurons and reactive astrocytes recruits circulating CCR2-positive Ly6C-high monocytes across a disrupted blood-spinal cord barrier, where they differentiate into neurotoxic macrophages, so CCR2 or CCL2 blockade will reduce infiltrate burden and motor neuron loss.

NF-κB-activated reactive astrocytes secrete TNF-α that engages TNFR1 (TNFRSF1A) on motor neurons, triggering caspase-8/3-mediated apoptotic signaling that compounds glutamate excitotoxicity, so TNF-α or TNFR1 blockade will protect motor neurons.

An imbalance in mitochondrial dynamics favoring DRP1 (DNM1L)-driven fission over OPA1/MFN2-mediated fusion fragments the mitochondrial network, reduces OXPHOS complex I/IV capacity, and produces organism-wide ATP bioenergetic failure.

Upregulation of the lncRNA NEAT1 in motor neurons acts as a competing endogenous RNA that sponges miR-124, derepressing miR-124 targets and shifting the transcriptome toward a degenerative, non-neuronal state in ALS.
